discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: moiré quantum materials and strongly correlated two-dimensional electron systems
motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted that twisting two graphene sheets to a 'magic' angle near 1.1 degrees would make the electronic bands nearly flat. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group realized this with a new tear-and-stack twist control. They found correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity in a single, gate-tunable carbon device. This created the field of twistronics, a new route to designing quantum matter. Interaction strength, band topology and filling can all be tuned in situ. Groups around the world, including those using spectroscopic imaging, have reproduced and extended these results. They showed cascades of symmetry-broken phases, nematicity, orbital magnetism, Chern insulators and, in related moiré systems, fractional quantum anomalous Hall states. This is a clear case of theoretical prediction followed by experimental ingenuity, and it gave condensed-matter physics a versatile platform for studying correlated and topological phases of electrons.
